name: Ukraine
who: Russia vs Ukraine, with the US mediating talks
what: Full-scale invasion, now a grinding war of attrition
when: Started Feb 24, 2022 — day 1,650+ and still going
how: Daily drone, missile and artillery strikes along a front over 1,100 km long
current: US-mediated peace talks have resumed, with Zelensky describing the first day as constructive, though progress remains limited to prisoner exchanges. Russian forces continue strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure, including a recent attack on Zaporizhzhia that injured 22 people and closed the DniproHES dam. Diplomatic friction persists as the US reportedly suggested Ukraine cede parts of Donbas for NATO membership, a claim Ukraine disputes.

sources.label: BBC News: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
Kyiv Post: Russian Strikes on Zaporizhzhia Injure 22, Kill 1 in Kushuhum
Al Jazeera: US suggested Ukraine cede parts of Donbas to Russia to become part of NATO
Al Jazeera: Three killed in Russia as Ukraine claims US floated NATO membership option

perspective.dominant_frame: Tier 1 sources like the BBC emphasize the constructive nature of the resumed US-mediated talks, while Tier 3 sources like Al Jazeera and Kyiv Post highlight the continued violence and the controversial US proposal regarding territorial concessions. Both tiers agree on the ongoing military strikes but diverge on the emphasis of diplomatic progress versus military reality.

escalation.note: Sustained Russian strikes on infrastructure and stalled diplomatic progress despite resumed talks.

name: Gaza
what: War technically under ceasefire, but violence continues
when: War since Oct 7, 2023; ceasefire since Oct 10, 2025
how: Over 1,300 people killed since the "ceasefire" began; disarmament and reconstruction stalled
current: The conflict remains in a state of high-intensity military operations, with recent reports detailing significant casualties among civilians, including children, during Israeli raids. While some sources reference earlier phases of the war involving hostage negotiations and infrastructure dismantling, the most recent verified data highlights ongoing lethal attacks on aid seekers and specific targets within Gaza.

sources.label: Al Jazeera: Latest Israeli attacks exacerbate hardships of life in Gaza
The Washington Post: Latest Israel-Hamas war news and Gaza conflict updates
Al Jazeera: Updates: Israeli troops kill 24, wound 200 in Gaza in latest aid attack

perspective.dominant_frame: Tier 1 sources like The Washington Post focus on strategic military phases, such as the dismantling of Hamas infrastructure and diplomatic efforts regarding hostages. Tier 3 sources like Al Jazeera emphasize the humanitarian impact, specifically highlighting high civilian casualty counts and the exacerbation of daily hardships due to military raids.

escalation.note: Recent strikes killed 45 Palestinians including 16 children, indicating sustained high-intensity violence.

name: Iran
who: Israel and the US vs Iran
what: A leadership-shattering war, now in an uneasy pause
how: US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s Supreme Leader; his son succeeded him; Hormuz still shut
current: The US and Iran are engaged in a cycle of retaliatory strikes, with Iran targeting US military assets in Bahrain and the US enforcing a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump has stated that large-scale strikes are unlikely due to 'positive momentum' and pressure from Gulf allies, while Iranian officials warn they may strike preemptively. Diplomatic efforts remain active but fragile, with the US reportedly no longer interested in a deal to end the war.

sources.label: AP News: Trump says he believes war with Iran is militarily 'effectively over'
Al Jazeera: Iran war live: Tehran warns it may strike first before another US attack
Al Jazeera: Iran war live: Trump says Gulf allies urged pause in Iran strikes
BBC News: US-Israel war with Iran | Latest News and Updates

perspective.dominant_frame: Tier 1 sources like AP and BBC focus on the US perspective of de-escalation, highlighting Trump's claims of military effectiveness and diplomatic momentum. Tier 3 sources like Al Jazeera emphasize the ongoing Iranian retaliation and warnings of preemptive strikes, framing the situation as a continuing cycle of violence despite diplomatic talk.

escalation.note: Active naval blockade and retaliatory drone strikes on US bases indicate sustained high-level conflict.

name: Sudan
who: Army (SAF) vs the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces
what: Civil war hardening into a formal partition
when: Since April 15, 2023, now in its 4th year
how: RSF controls Darfur and the west; army holds the center, north and east
current: The conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) continues with sustained violence, including recent drone strikes that have reportedly killed over 1,000 civilians this year. The humanitarian crisis has deepened, with the WFP warning of widespread famine and millions displaced, while RSF forces and allied militias have committed mass atrocities in western Darfur. Despite diplomatic efforts, the war remains unresolved with no ceasefire in place.

sources.label: UN News: Aid is the ‘only hope’ for millions in Sudan, WFP chief warns, as funding cuts deepen hunger crisis
CFR: Civil War in Sudan | Global Conflict Tracker
DPPA: Remarks by ASG Kimani at the General Assembly Fourth Committee on special political missions
UNHCR: THE SUDAN EMERGENCY: THREE YEARS ON | 2025 UPDATE

perspective.dominant_frame: Sources uniformly frame the situation as a catastrophic humanitarian and security crisis, emphasizing the scale of civilian casualties from drone strikes and the severity of the famine. The focus is on the failure of diplomatic efforts to achieve a ceasefire and the ongoing mass atrocities, particularly in Darfur. There is no divergence in the core narrative of a high-intensity civil war with severe humanitarian consequences.

escalation.note: Sustained drone strikes killing 1,000+ civilians and mass atrocities in Darfur indicate critical escalation.

name: Sahel (Mali)
who: Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and allied fighters vs the military government
what: Jihadist fuel blockade and insurgency threatening the junta
when: Blockade of the capital began around September 2025
how: Fuel convoys attacked, schools and businesses paralyzed; blockade has since eased somewhat
current: Mali is on the brink of civil war as Islamist groups and Tuareg rebels consolidate power in the north, with violence more than doubling since the first phase of UN peacekeeper withdrawal in August. JNIM has launched a renewed offensive, shifting its strategy from rural areas to targeting major cities, including coordinated attacks on government forces and military bases in Bamako. The conflict has been further complicated by the emergence of a separatist-al-Qaeda alliance and deadly clashes between JNIM and IS-Sahel.

sources.label: CFR: Violent Extremism in the Sahel
UN News: Guterres calls for international solutions to curb spread of violent extremism in the Sahel
Al Jazeera: How armed group alliances are reshaping Mali’s conflict and the wider Sahel
International Crisis Group: Mali

perspective.dominant_frame: Sources consistently frame the situation as a critical escalation driven by the UN withdrawal and the consolidation of power by JNIM and Tuareg rebels. Tier 2 sources (CFR, Crisis Group) emphasize the structural shift toward civil war and the specific tactical changes by JNIM, while Tier 3 (Al Jazeera) highlights the complex web of alliances, including the role of Russian forces and separatist groups. There is no significant divergence on the severity of the situation, with all sources agreeing on the intensification of violence.

escalation.note: Violence more than doubled since UN withdrawal; JNIM targeting major cities; brink of civil war.

name: Myanmar
who: Military junta vs resistance fighters and ethnic armed groups
what: Civil war following the 2021 coup, now with a civilian facade
when: Coup Feb 1, 2021; Min Aung Hlaing elected president April 3, 2026
how: Junta-backed party swept a sham election; war with resistance forces continues in the borderlands
current: Myanmar’s civil war has entered a stalemate, with resistance forces controlling an estimated 42 percent of the country against the junta’s 21 percent. The humanitarian situation has deteriorated further, with over 5.2 million people displaced and the military conducting renewed offensives in Rakhine State. Recent reports document deliberate targeting of civilian sites, including double-tap airstrikes and attacks on markets and villages that have killed dozens.

sources.label: CFR: Civil War in Myanmar | Global Conflict Tracker
France 24: Myanmar: Junta carries out double-tap airstrikes targeting civilians
Crisis Group: Myanmar
UNHCR: Situation Myanmar Situation

perspective.dominant_frame: Sources uniformly frame the conflict as a humanitarian catastrophe driven by the junta's intensified military offensives, particularly in Rakhine State. While Western outlets emphasize the brutality of double-tap strikes and civilian casualties, regional and analytical sources also highlight the diplomatic stalemate and the US strategy linking peace talks to rare-earth access.

escalation.note: Renewed military offensive in Rakhine with documented double-tap airstrikes and mass displacement.

name: Venezuela
who: US military vs Maduro; now a US-backed government vs the opposition
what: Maduro captured in a US raid, transition still in limbo
when: Raid on Jan 3, 2026; still no election date set
how: Acting president installed with US backing; opposition leader repeatedly blocked from returning
current: The US has formally charged ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores with torture and abuse of Americans, expanding previous indictments. Diplomatic efforts continue as Secretary of State Marco Rubio engages in talks regarding a legal agreement, while exiled opposition leader Maria Corina Machado was blocked from re-entering the country. Domestic political tensions in the US are rising, with impeachment proceedings against Secretary of Defense Hegseth citing the abduction of Maduro as an unauthorized act of war.

Al Jazeera: US charges Venezuela’s Nicolas Maduro over torture allegations

escalation.note: Regime collapse is complete with Maduro in US detention, but high tension persists due to new torture charges and US domestic impeachment battles.

name: E. DR Congo

what: Peace deals signed, but M23 still controls the ground
when: Washington and Doha deals signed mid-2025; conflict decades old

current: Violence in eastern DR Congo has intensified, with IS-linked gunmen killing at least 44 civilians in Ituri province and 33 in North Kivu this week. Concurrently, the Congolese military has sentenced 66 soldiers to death for cowardice and desertion during clashes with rebels. These events occur against a backdrop of a severe Ebola outbreak that has killed over 5,300 people, straining humanitarian and security resources.

Al Jazeera: Armed men kill at least 33 in village in Ebola-hit eastern DRC

Tier 3 sources like Africanews and Al Jazeera focus on the immediate humanitarian impact of IS-linked attacks and the concurrent Ebola crisis. Both tiers agree on the severity of the violence but differ in emphasis between military discipline and civilian casualties.

escalation.note: Sustained IS-linked attacks killing dozens and mass death sentences for soldiers indicate high-intensity conflict.

name: Taiwan Strait
who: China (PLA) vs Taiwan, with the US and Japan backing Taipei
what: Escalating military pressure just short of open conflict
how: Record Chinese aircraft and ship incursions into Taiwan’s air defense zone
current: Xi Jinping has asserted that Taiwan's 'complete reunification' with China is inevitable, a statement made ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Concurrently, the Taiwanese Ministry of National Defence reported a significant reduction in Chinese military activity, with only one aircraft and eight ships detected near Taiwan between November 8 and 9, down from 49 flights on November 3. Analysts describe the status quo as precarious, with Beijing flexing military muscles while Washington sends mixed signals.

France 24: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
Crisis Group: Taiwan Strait

perspective.dominant_frame: Sources frame the situation as a period of heightened rhetorical tension from Beijing, with Xi Jinping's reunification statement serving as a key driver. This is juxtaposed with reports of a tangible decrease in immediate military pressure, as Chinese aircraft and ship counts near Taiwan have dropped significantly. The Crisis Group characterizes the overall status quo as precarious due to political discord in Taipei and mixed signals from Washington.

escalation.note: Xi's explicit reunification rhetoric elevates tension despite a reported drop in daily military activity near the strait.

what: Nuclear and missile buildup, with no active dialogue
how: Repeated launches; Pyongyang calls Seoul a "hostile enemy state"
current: Tensions on the Korean Peninsula remain high following a series of provocative actions, including North Korea's launch of multiple ballistic missiles and a new cluster warhead test. South Korea is investigating the death of a frontline soldier near the border, adding to the strain caused by recent landmine explosions that injured three soldiers. While Seoul has proposed talks to officially end the war, Pyongyang has rejected border negotiations and condemned joint US-South Korean military drills as rehearsals for aggressive war.

The situation remains tense with ongoing diplomatic friction between Manila and Beijing.

how: Missile, drone and artillery exchange; US-mediated ceasefire holds, dispute unresolved
current: The India-Pakistan ceasefire established after the May 2025 military conflict remains in effect, though diplomatic relations and trust remain frozen. Recent violence in Pakistan-administered Kashmir has been driven by clashes between security forces and supporters of a banned protest group, resulting in at least 15 deaths. India continues to accuse Pakistan of sponsoring the militants responsible for the April 2025 Pahalgam attack, an allegation Pakistan denies.

Regional dynamics are further complicated by the strategic significance of the South Caucasus in the context of the Iran war.

Thailand has moved to block fuel supplies to Cambodia as hostilities continue despite a ceasefire agreement reached in December. Recent incidents include accusations of ceasefire breaches involving drones and ongoing artillery exchanges along the 800km border.

U.S. officials have urged restraint and dialogue to prevent the widening of the conflict in the Horn of Africa.
